full_judgment:
Mr. A. M. Mahmudur Rahman, J:-This petition for leave to appeal by the plaintiff-petitioners is from the judgment and order dated 22.3.99 passed by the High Court Division in First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 249 of 1997. 

 2. The plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 89 of 1997 for declaration that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 14 of 1960 was fraudulent and illegal and for partition of the disputed property stating that the said decree put into execution in Execution Case No. 10 of 1992 cannot be executed as the property under the decree was in joint possession of the plaintiffs and the defendants and that the defendants were trying to possess the land of plot. No. 45 forcibly. 

 3. In the said suit the plaintiffs filed an application for temporary injunction which was resisted by the defendants stating that the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs and that of the defendants got a contested decree in Partition Suit No. 14 of 1960 and that the defendants are entitled to get possession in satisfaction of the decree through the Execution Case which they filed in the executing court. 

 5. The learned Judges of the High Court Division found on material evidence on record that the plaintiffs failed to make out a prima facie case for injunction and that the decree obtained in a contested suit put in execution for satisfaction of the decree cannot be defeated on the ground the defendants are out to take possession forcibly of the land covered by the contested decree and upon such findings allowed the appeal with cost setting aside the order dated 24.7.1997 passed by the trial court granting injunction. 

 7. In an application under Order 39 rule 1 C.P.C. the precise question needs to be decided is whether the plaintiffs proved a prima facie case in his favour to obtain an order of injunction. In the instant case the learned Judges of the High Court Division rightly found that the plaintiffs failed to prove so. An order of injunction is not to issue merely on the plea of the plaintiffs that the defendants are trying to take forcibly possession of the property in a case where the defendants put the contested decree in execution for satisfaction of such decree.
